results.name: The phone was compromised before the user turned it on: the rise of Midnight Mimosa
results.description: A sophisticated malware campaign targets low-cost Android devices built on MediaTek platforms, with malicious code preinstalled in device firmware before users receive them. The platform-signed system application operates with elevated privileges, enabling operators to silently install applications, grant permissions, and load remote code. The scheme primarily generates revenue through ad fraud, click fraud, device information collection, and converting infected devices into residential-proxy botnet nodes. The malicious system application ships under various system-sounding names including com.android.system.lite, com.android.sys.prot, and com.android.sys.gmsprot. Operators deploy at least 32 disguised applications including fake weather, app-lock, and OCR tools. The malware disables Google Play Store during payload installation to evade detection, then re-enables it afterward. Thirteen related applications were also discovered on Google Play, communicating with identical command-and-control infrastructure...

results.name: From WhatsApp to SYSTEM: Inside the VulcanRAT207.A Intrusion Chain
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage intrusion chain begins with a WhatsApp-delivered financial document lure carrying Statement.exe. The malware employs NRV2E compression to conceal its true payload, which performs extensive host screening before attempting privilege elevation via COM-based techniques. Using PoolParty Variant 7 injection, the loader transfers execution into the Windows Task Scheduler process under LocalSystem authority. A downloader shellcode retrieves a compound bundle from a remote server, which deploys through a reflective loader. The deployment stage utilizes a signed GoFly driver to terminate Baidu security processes, establishes persistence via DLL side-loading with a legitimate Intel-signed VulkanInfo executable, and launches a WebSocket-based remote access trojan. The final VulcanRAT207.A payload provides extensive surveillance capabilities including shell access, keystroke capture, desktop control, network filtering, and process injection, while maintaining persistence through SYSTEM-leve...

results.name: From Endpoint to Funhouse: Changes in Ransomware Families and Kimsuky-Related Distribution Cases
results.description: A North Korean threat actor distributed Funhouse ransomware through malicious Korean-language documents disguised as resumes. Funhouse is a variant of the previously observed Endpoint ransomware. The attack chain involves multi-stage scripts including Batch, VBS, and PowerShell, leading to Quasar RAT installation before deploying the final ransomware payload. The campaign shares significant similarities with earlier Kimsuky Endpoint ransomware operations from early 2026, including identical mutex values, similar batch file structures, and comparable Quasar RAT configurations. The ransomware maintains key characteristics of the Endpoint family while updating encryption extensions, contact information, and C2 infrastructure. A notable shift involves using HWP documents instead of LNK files as initial infection vectors.

results.name: Inside a brand deal scam targeting YouTube creators
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign targets YouTube content creators through personalized sponsorship emails impersonating legitimate brands like Hollyland, Nike, and Spotify. Attackers send customized collaboration offers referencing specific videos from targets' channels, then direct them to fraudulent platforms that appear legitimate with campaign metrics and income calculators. The scheme culminates in a Google sign-in request that either captures credentials directly or requests excessive account permissions. Once compromised, attackers lock victims out by changing recovery methods and can misuse the account to spread scams to followers. The modular campaign operates globally, targeting creators in Peru, Japan, and English-speaking regions, using multiple domains while maintaining similar functionality and design patterns across variants.

results.name: Threat Overview: NetScaler Zero Days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Being Exploited in Production Environments (Updated September 30)
results.description: Two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway systems are being actively exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-88771 is a remote code execution vulnerability allowing unauthenticated command injection, while CVE-2026-88772 is a DTLS memory overflow flaw enabling RCE or DoS attacks. Threat actors deployed webshells through these vulnerabilities to establish initial access and persistence. The CVE-2026-88771 exploitation involves a three-stage command injection chain poisoning log files, while CVE-2026-88772 exploitation drops .deb webshell files. Attackers used PHP webshells with RC4 encryption for command and control communications, targeting custom directories within NetScaler Gateway interfaces. Cortex Xpanse identified over 50,000 potentially vulnerable exposed instances.

results.name: DNS as C2 in Noir, An AI-Developed Crypto Wallet Drainer
results.description: A cryptocurrency wallet-drainer kit called Noir uses DNS TXT records and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) as a dynamic command-and-control mechanism. The loader queries public DoH services to discover active infrastructure hosted on Cloudflare Pages, allowing operators to redirect deployed lures by changing a single DNS record. The drainer does not require victims to enter seed phrases or private keys; instead, it requests wallet connection permissions and obtains spending approvals that appear less suspicious than direct transfers. The architecture separates long-lived phishing lures from short-lived operational infrastructure, with 60-second DNS caching and self-healing retry logic. Extensive plain-English code comments suggest AI-assisted development, documenting bugs, fixes, and design decisions. The kit serves as a shared service across multiple cryptocurrency-themed phishing campaigns.

results.name: The Scalpel vs. The Sledgehammer: Lessons in Precision Triage from the .conf26 SOC
results.description: During a live Security Operations Center shift at .conf26 in Denver, analysts investigated Incident ES_00244 involving an exploit link detected by Cisco Secure Firewall. The challenge arose when 15 devices were found communicating with a single IP address (13.226.251.40) flagged for hosting malicious domains moonlighthathel[.]org and ukankingwithea[.]com. Investigation revealed the IP was an Amazon CloudFront CDN node simultaneously serving legitimate services including Samsung Health, Mindtickle learning platform, and Amazon Video. Using AI-assisted analysis, firewall logs, and packet forensics through Endace, analysts isolated one unmanaged Intel laptop generating malicious traffic among 14 benign connections. Instead of blocking the shared IP and disrupting legitimate services, analysts implemented precise DNS object blocks targeting only the malicious domains at the Cisco Firepower Threat Defense perimeter, successfully neutralizing the threat while maintaining normal operations for all other attendees.

results.name: Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Exposes 30,000 Users' OAuth Tokens to Russian Bot Service
results.description: A malicious browser extension called 'Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot' distributed on Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons captures and forwards users' live Twitch OAuth session tokens to Russian-controlled proxy servers. The extension, with approximately 30,000 Chrome users and 552 Firefox users, markets itself as a quality-of-life tool for blocking ads and unlocking streams. While delivering these features, it secretly extracts users' account-scoped OAuth tokens and forwards them as query parameters to operator-controlled infrastructure. Current versions append tokens inline during video playlist redirects, while earlier builds explicitly POSTed tokens to dedicated collection endpoints. The operator is identified as a commercial Russian bot service called JeetBot, with infrastructure hosted across German and cloud providers.

results.name: KATARU: IoT Malware Adopts Public LPE Exploits
results.description: KATARU is an IoT malware variant discovered in August 2026 through Telnet credential brute-forcing against a honeypot from Vietnam. While maintaining traditional Mirai-style botnet capabilities, it distinguishes itself through an extensive feature set including multiple Linux local privilege escalation exploits, comprehensive persistence mechanisms across Linux and embedded platforms, encrypted C2 communications using X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, anti-analysis techniques, and decoy traffic generation. Implementation artifacts strongly suggest AI-assisted development, evidenced by architecture-mismatched x86 shellcode in ARM binaries, RFC test vectors as configuration values, and untested cross-platform persistence logic. The malware attempts various privilege escalation paths through system misconfigurations and public exploits, establishes persistence across numerous startup mechanisms, and supports multiple DDoS attack vectors alongside SSH brute-forcing capabilities.

results.name: Artifactory Under Attack: In-the-Wild Exploitation of CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018 & CVE-2026-82329
results.description: Active exploitation of three critical vulnerabilities in JFrog Artifactory has been identified, with attackers chaining CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018, and CVE-2026-82329 to bypass authentication and gain administrative control. CVE-2026-42018 exposes internal anonymous-user tokens, CVE-2026-42016 enables privilege escalation through insufficient token validation, and CVE-2026-82329 allows unauthenticated access to administrative privileges. Post-exploitation activities include creating persistent administrator accounts, deploying malicious Groovy plugins for code execution, and installing Rust-based backdoors. Exploitation was observed between August 15 and September 8, 2026, affecting multiple organizations. Data indicates 67-69% of organizations running Artifactory had vulnerable instances at initial publication, with slow patching velocity for lower-severity CVEs despite active exploitation across environments.
